title: First-order Kähler commutators with the dual Lefschetz operator
statement: Work over the complex field $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $M$ be a complex manifold without boundary, of complex dimension $n\geq0$, with a smooth positive definite Hermitian metric $h$ on its tangent bundle. Write $J$ for the complex structure, $g=\operatorname{Re}h$ for the underlying Riemannian metric, and $\omega(u,v)=g(Ju,v)$ for its associated real $(1,1)$-form. Assume $d\omega=0$. Write $A^k(M;\mathbf C)$ for smooth complex differential forms, and $A^{p,q}(M)$ for the type subspaces, with spaces outside $0\leq p,q\leq n$ zero. Let $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ be exterior differentiation decomposed by type. Let $\partial^*$ and $\bar\partial^*$ be their formal adjoints for the metric on complex forms and the volume of $g$: $\int_M\langle Du,v\rangle\,dV_g=\int_M\langle u,D^*v\rangle\,dV_g$ for compactly supported smooth test forms of the appropriate degrees, where $D=\partial$ or $\bar\partial$. Define $L\alpha=\omega\wedge\alpha$ and let $\Lambda:A^k\to A^{k-2}$ be the pointwise Hermitian adjoint of $L$, characterized by $\langle L\alpha,\beta\rangle_x=\langle\alpha,\Lambda\beta\rangle_x$ at every $x\in M$. On all smooth complex forms, with the ordinary commutator $[P,Q]=P\circ Q-Q\circ P$, one has $$[\Lambda,\partial]=i\bar\partial^*,\qquad [\Lambda,\bar\partial]=-i\partial^*.$$ Here $i^2=-1$. These are identities of differential operators, without compactness or completeness assumptions.

source.place: WANTED locally: Wenrui Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §6.4, Definition 6.10, Lemma 6.11 and the first-order commutator identities of Proposition 6.12, printed p.26 (PDF page 26); read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf.

proof.text: If $n=0$, positive-degree forms and all the operators in question vanish, so both identities hold. Otherwise fix $a\in M$ and choose the chart of [lem-sfb-kahler-normal-holomorphic-coordinates]. At $a$, $g$ is Euclidean and its first coordinate derivatives vanish. The matrices of the induced metrics on all exterior powers, the density $\rho=\sqrt{\det g}$, and the coefficients of $\Lambda$ have vanishing first derivatives there: the inverse-metric entries, determinant and exterior-power minors are smooth functions of the metric entries, so their derivatives are zero by the chain rule. Thus the product rule for differentiating $\Lambda\alpha$ has no term involving a derivative of $\Lambda$ at $a$.

source.place: §3.3 Theorem 3.19 and §6.4 Proposition 6.12, normal-coordinate reduction; derivative consequences written out by the agent

proof.text: Set $e_j=dz_j/\sqrt2$ and $b_j=d\bar z_j/\sqrt2$. These are an orthonormal complex cotangent basis at $a$. In the coordinate exterior basis let $E_j,B_j$ be left wedge by $e_j,b_j$, and $I_j,K_j$ the constant coefficient contractions with their dual basis vectors. Contraction deletes an occurrence in position $l$ with sign $(-1)^{l-1}$, and is zero when it is absent. Comparing orthonormal wedge monomials shows $E_j^*=I_j$, $B_j^*=K_j$ at $a$. The deletion rule gives $I_jE_k+E_kI_j=\delta_{jk}$, $K_jB_k+B_kK_j=\delta_{jk}$, and zero mixed anticommutators. Hence $[K_jI_j,E_k]=\delta_{jk}K_j$ and $[K_jI_j,B_k]=-\delta_{jk}I_j$: expand $K_j(I_jE_k)$ and $(K_jB_k)I_j$ using those relations. Since $\omega(a)=i\sum_j e_j\wedge b_j$, taking conjugate-transpose matrices gives $\Lambda(a)=-i\sum_j K_jI_j$. Therefore $$[\Lambda(a),E_k]=-iK_k,\qquad[\Lambda(a),B_k]=iI_k.$$

source.place: §6.4 Definition 6.10, Lemma 6.11 and Proposition 6.12; agent writes out the exterior-basis calculation

proof.text: On coefficient functions in this fixed exterior frame, $\partial=\sqrt2\sum_j E_j\partial_{z_j}$ and $\bar\partial=\sqrt2\sum_j B_j\partial_{\bar z_j}$. Apply [lem-sfb-first-order-local-formal-adjoint] with the induced exterior metrics and density $\rho$ of step 1. They are smooth and positive, and their first derivatives vanish at $a$; the displayed wedge matrices are constant and the zeroth-order coefficient is zero. Substituting $\partial_z=(\partial_x-i\partial_y)/2$ into that formula conjugates $-i$ to $i$ when taking an adjoint, so $$ (\partial^*\alpha)(a)=-\sqrt2\sum_j I_j(\partial_{\bar z_j}\alpha)(a),\qquad (\bar\partial^*\alpha)(a)=-\sqrt2\sum_j K_j(\partial_{z_j}\alpha)(a). $$ The cited local uniqueness and chart compatibility identify these with the formal adjoints specified in the item, for arbitrary smooth $\alpha$.

source.place: §6.1 Lemma 6.2 and §6.4 Proposition 6.12; agent derives the pointwise adjoint formulas from the weighted local formula

proof.text: Using the vanished coefficient derivatives of step 1, apply the product rule to both commutators. Step 2 gives $$([\Lambda,\partial]\alpha)(a)=\sqrt2\sum_j[\Lambda(a),E_j](\partial_{z_j}\alpha)(a)=-i\sqrt2\sum_jK_j(\partial_{z_j}\alpha)(a)=i(\bar\partial^*\alpha)(a),$$ and $$([\Lambda,\bar\partial]\alpha)(a)=\sqrt2\sum_j[\Lambda(a),B_j](\partial_{\bar z_j}\alpha)(a)=i\sqrt2\sum_jI_j(\partial_{\bar z_j}\alpha)(a)=-i(\partial^*\alpha)(a).$$ This computes the full operators at the point, including zeroth-order terms. The point $a$ and smooth form $\alpha$ were arbitrary, proving both identities globally. Exterior wedge and contraction already vanish beyond the degree range, so the same calculation includes boundary bidegrees.

source.place: §6.4 Proposition 6.12, first-order identities; agent completes the local calculation and pointwise conclusion

proof_origin.place: Kong Theorem 3.19, Lemmas 6.2 and 6.11, Proposition 6.12, read online; WANTED locally. Agent expands the normal-coordinate proof idea using the general weighted formal-adjoint formula.
